subject: quantitative_aptitude
question: Find the number of integral values of m for which the quadratic equation (m - 2)x^2 - (m + 4)x + 2m - 1 = 0 has both roots strictly greater than 1.
explanation: For (m - 2)x^2 - (m + 4)x + (2m - 1) = 0 to have both roots strictly greater than 1: (1) Discriminant D >= 0: -7m^2 + 28m + 8 >= 0 => m in [-0.27, 4.27]. (2) (m - 2)f(1) > 0: (m - 2)(2m - 7) > 0 => m < 2 or m > 3.5. (3) Axis of symmetry -b/(2a) > 1: (m + 4)/[2(m - 2)] > 1 => for m > 2, m + 4 > 2m - 4 => m < 8; for m < 2, m + 4 < 2m - 4 => m > 8 (impossible). Testing integers in [-0.27, 4.27]: {0, 1, 2, 3, 4}. Integers 0 and 1 fail vertex condition; 2 makes it linear; 3 fails condition 2. Only m = 4 satisfies all conditions (roots of 2x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0 are 2.707 and 1.293, both > 1). Thus, exactly 1 integral value exists.
